text_summary.body: The leaders and all whom God stirred rose to go up and build; neighbours gave silver, gold, goods and animals. Cyrus brought out the vessels Nebuchadnezzar had placed in his gods' house; Mithredath counted them to Sheshbazzar: 30 gold dishes, 1,000 silver dishes, 29 knives, 30 gold bowls, 410 silver bowls, 1,000 other vessels — "all … were five thousand four hundred"; Sheshbazzar brought them up with the exiles.

setting.body: The Cyrus Cylinder records Cyrus returning gods' images to their sanctuaries; Judah, which had no images, is not named. Josephus retells the episode with Mithridates and Sanabassar and has Cyrus's letter name Zorobabel as governor.

terminology.gloss: Sheshbazzar's title; Ezra 5:14 calls him governor (peḥâ).

competing_reconstructions.label: Sheshbazzar = Zerubbabel
proponents: Clarke (Chaldean name) and Kidner (official name), via Guzik
competing_reconstructions.summary: Both are said to lay the foundation (Ezra 3:8–10; 5:16).

competing_reconstructions.label: Two different leaders
competing_reconstructions.summary: Sheshbazzar led the first return; Zerubbabel led the later rebuilding; Josephus names both Sanabassar and Zorobabel.

competing_reconstructions.label: The vessels: returned intact, or only those not destroyed
competing_reconstructions.summary: 2 Kgs 24:13 says the gold vessels were cut in pieces; Dan 5:2–3 has vessels used at Belshazzar's feast; Poole reconciles the "cut in pieces" statement.

commentary.paraphrase: Guzik stresses that only a "spirit-stirred minority" returned and notes the views that Sheshbazzar was Zerubbabel or a distinct official.

open_questions: Which list is original — Ezra's items (2,499) or 1 Esdras's (5,469)?
